issue_context.title: Rewrite zwave unittest tests to pytest style test functions
issue_context.body:
## Problem

The zwave integration still contains `unittest.TestCase` based unit tests. We want to rewrite them to standalone pytest test functions.

## Background

The Home Assistant core standard is to write tests as standalone pytest test functions. We still have some old tests that are based on `unittest.TestCase`. We want all these tests to be rewritten as pytest test functions.

Here are the docs for pytest: https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/

Here's an example of an async pytest test function in Home Assistant core:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4cce724473233d4fb32c08bd251940b1ce2ba570/tests/components/tradfri/test_light.py#L156-L176

There are many pytest fixtures to help writing the tests. See:

- https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference.html#fixtures
- https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/tests/conftest.py
- The most common fixture to use is [`hass`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4cce724473233d4fb32c08bd251940b1ce2ba570/tests/conftest.py#L107) which will set up a [`HomeAssistant`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4cce724473233d4fb32c08bd251940b1ce2ba570/homeassistant/core.py#L166) instance and start it.

Here's an example of a pull request that rewrote a module of `unittest.TestCase` tests to standalone pytest test functions:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/40749

Here's an example command to run a single test module with pytest inside tox on Python 3.8:

```sh
tox -e py38 -- --cov-report term-missing --cov=homeassistant.components.command_line.switch tests/components/command_line/test_switch.py
```

It will print coverage information with lines that are missing coverage.

## Prerequisites

- A working [development environment](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_environment).

## Task

- Rewrite the tests one module at a time and submit the changes as a pull request to this repository.
- We want to limit the change scope to a single module to not have the pull request be too long, which would take longer time to review.
- Remember to reference this issue in your pull request, but don't close or fix the issue until all tests for the integration are updated.
comments: I made a pass at this linked above by using `pytest.fixture` instead of the setup and teardown method. Happy to submit a PR if this is the kind of thing you were looking for.
@jeffaudio please make a PR so we can see what you did.
Submitted the PR as requested. Looks like there's another one out there so feel that took a slightly different route so feel free to close mine if it's not what you wanted.
I'm working on `test_init.py`, that seems to be the only one left with `unittest.TestCase` inside.

review_comments: We should be able to get the network from the `mock_openzwave` mock, ie `mock_openzwave.network.ZWaveNetwork.return_value`.

Any idea why it fails?

```
        zwave_network = mock_openzwave.network.ZWaveNetwork.return_value
>       zwave_network.state = MockNetwork.STATE_READY
E       AttributeError: 'property' object has no attribute 'state'
```
Not directly. I'd check how the mocking is done.
We can improve this later if it's tricky.

I'm close to giving up. This is as far as I come.

The `mock_openzwave` patches `openzwave.network`:

```
base_mock.network.ZWaveNetwork = MockNetwork
    base_mock.option.ZWaveOption = MockOption

    with patch.dict(
        "sys.modules",
        {
            "libopenzwave": libopenzwave,
            "openzwave.option": base_mock.option,
            "openzwave.network": base_mock.network,
            "openzwave.group": base_mock.group,
        },
    ):
        yield base_mock
```

In `__init__.py` it creates an instance of ZWaveNetwork:

`network = hass.data[DATA_NETWORK] = ZWaveNetwork(options, autostart=False)`

Is it even possible to get the instance through `mock_openzwave`?
I think we'd need to change how we patch the library. We can do that in the future. There's a lot to clean up about the existing zwave tests still.

Is there a need to do that? I may clean it up some more, but I need some direction what should be cleaned up.

Generally I think existing tests, at least in `test_init` can be cleaned up further by using the new fixtures introduced. I also found two instances where `caplog` could be used.

We should set up the integration and avoid interacting with integration details in the tests.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_testing#writing-tests-for-integrations

The zwave tests are currently not written like that.
Python dictionaries are ordered by default from Python 3.7 so this test is a bit weird. I'd remove this test.
